newsitem.title: NORWAY: POLL-Dyno H197 pre-tax seen up 18 pct.
newsitem.headline: POLL-Dyno H197 pre-tax seen up 18 pct.

text.p: Norwegian explosives and chemicals group Dyno Industrier ASA is expected to present a pre-tax profit of 218 million crowns in the first six months of 1997, according to a Reuters poll of seven Norwegian analysts.
The first half 1996, Dyno booked profits before tax of 184 million crowns.
Three of the analysts recommended to buy the stock, three said hold and one said sell.

As usual, the analysts said they would focus on Dyno's margins and the price of raw materials. There also was considerable interest in how far the company had gone in its restructuring programme dubbed Dyno 2000, they said.
Some of the analysts saw a squeeze on margins in Dyno's chemical division.
"It is definitely the case in Asia," commented one.
Another said: "I have spoken with a few of Dyno's customers in Europe and they say that prices for resins have come down."
Results for chemicals is first and foremost expected to be underpinned by higher methanol prices.
"They should also begin to show higher margins in the explosives business," another analysts said, adding that ammonia -- a raw material in the production of explosives -- prices had fallen.
